conflicts.fact: Mutual exclusivity of Gor Mahia match outcomes and what the P(Win), P(Draw), P(Loss) values are
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 treats a single match as having WIN/DRAW/LOSE each with probability 1/3 (equally likely), giving P(Win or Draw)=2/3, while Lesson 1 asks whether a football match is even an equally likely event and Lesson 7 models a match as WIN/LOSE at 0.5 and Lesson 8 uses a P=0.216 (0.6^3) three-match case; the sequence gives incompatible probability models for the same match.

conflicts.fact: Length of Gor Mahia winning streak
conflicts.versions: Lessons 1, 2, 4, 6 predict phase and Lesson 7 use a streak of 7 wins; Lesson 6's Explained/Learned summary says a 'five-win streak' and 'match six'.

conflicts.fact: Number of Lesson 6 summary conflicts: 'seven consecutive wins' vs 'eighth match'
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 overview refers to seven consecutive wins and the eighth match, but Lesson 6 Explained refers to a five-win streak and match six.

conflicts.fact: Whether 'Gor Mahia win AND draw' / 'both teams winning' is covered consistently, and the claim that mutually exclusive events have probability zero
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 says P(A and B)=0 for mutually exclusive events; Lesson 8 says mutually exclusive events (both teams winning the same match) have a combined probability of zero, fine, but Lesson 4's Overview says 'bettor picks Gor Mahia to win AND to draw' then later describes P(Win or Draw)=2/3 as exploiting that 'losses accumulate' versus Lesson 5 saying advertisers blur mutual exclusivity; the lessons disagree on why the advert is misleading.

conflicts.fact: Class coin-toss data from Lesson 1 used in Lesson 3 vs. what was recorded
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 records a pooled class table of 40 tosses per pair; Lesson 3 says it uses a 'class coin-toss frequency table accumulated in Lesson 1' as evidence for 0-1 range, whereas Lesson 3's activities show only Evidence Cards (maize, fruit, dice, spinner).

conflicts.fact: Number of trials in the independent-events experiment and description
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 uses 24 coin-and-die trials; Lesson 7 says the 'WIN–WIN' experiment used 20 trials with Lesson 7 Observed saying coin tossed twice in 20 trials, and Lesson 7 Learned says the betting stall payout uses 180 spins at P(win)=1/3 collecting Ksh 3,600 (Ksh 20 per spin) with expected payout Ksh 1,800 implying payout of Ksh 30 per win, an unstated inconsistent figure.

conflicts.fact: Probability that Gor Mahia wins used in multiplication examples
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 uses P(win)=0.5 for a simplified match and 1/3 for the stall; Lesson 8 Scenario 4 uses P=0.216 (i.e. 0.6 per match for three matches), giving different win probabilities for the same team.
